quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which formation keeps riders in a group closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps a group close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: After a motorcycle helmet is in a crash, it should be:
questions.explanation: Replace any helmet that has been in a crash.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see the cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see the cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign as indicated. Then edge forward and stop again before the cross traffic lane. Lean your body forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for approaching traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Usually results in no difference in handling a motorcycle.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Can affect the handling of a motorcycle.
Is encouraged to get operators used to different riding situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect the handling of a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight and changes how the motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: If you are riding alongside another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit and then exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or drop back to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: To lower the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you and understand your plans. Use proper signaling and lane positioning. Keep a good space cushion and watch for hazards ahead so you can react.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently as part of normal scanning. Also check them before changing lanes, when stopping at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: A group of riders should merge onto a highway in:
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation during normal riding. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front or rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close while staying safe?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving each rider enough space to stay safe. Use single-file when turning, in curves, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It uses more of the road surface.
It limits your escape routes if something happens.
It makes it easier to talk to the other rider.
It makes it easier for cars to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if something happens.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcycle. This limits both riders' options to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Leave more space when stopping takes longer. Increase your distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: A good eye or face shield should have all of these features except:
questions.explanation: Good eye protection must be free of scratches, resist piercing, give clear side vision, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. Extra weight requires more braking force to stop. Stopping takes longer when going downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: Which fabric gives motorcyclists the most protection?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of riding experience. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to road hazards ahead.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, how does acceleration and stopping change?

options.text: It takes less time to accelerate but more time to stop.
It takes more time to accelerate and stop.
It takes more time to accelerate but less time to stop.
It takes less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Added weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to speed up and to stop.

questions.question: A thorough check of your motorcycle:

options.text: Only works if a mechanic does it.
Should not be done before riding.
Should only be done after riding.
Can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find problems that could be dangerous.

questions.question: For routine braking:

options.text: Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Always use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which protects your eyes from wind the best?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: Your body removes about one drink per hour. If someone drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours, how many drinks stay in their system 3 hours after their last drink?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. Example: 7 drinks consumed in 3 hours means 4 drinks remain 3 hours later.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. This usually takes only a few minutes.
